title: CheMLFlow: An Open-Source Platform for Cheminformatics and Materials Informatics Applications
authors: Brendan Smith, Susana Lopez-Moreno, Eric Dolores-Cuenca, Sangil Kim, Jose L. Mendoza-Cortes, Nijamudheen Abdulrahiman
abstract: CheMLFlow is an open-source platform for building and executing end-to-end, high-throughput, and agentic workflows for scientific and technological applications. CheMLFlow targets a common bottleneck in scientific machine learning development, where researchers often need to assemble data acquisition, curation, representation, model training, validation, screening, interpretation, and reporting into a reproducible pipeline, even when their primary research contribution concerns only one stage. CheMLFlow provides modular workflow components, ready-to-run reference pipelines, standardized artifacts, and evaluation outputs that reduce orchestration overhead and support benchmarking across methods and datasets. The platform is designed to be extensible, reproducible, and automation friendly, with pluggable representations and models, deterministic splits, explicit run artifacts, batch execution, and report generation. As scientific software increasingly moves toward agent assisted experimentation, CheMLFlow's configuration driven workflows and structured outputs also provide a practical interface for coding agents to help users construct experiments, inspect results, and summarize findings under human supervision. This article describes the system architecture, core workflows, and benchmarks that reach literature performance for quantum mechanical, physicochemical and bioactivity property prediction, and use cases involving time series datasets demonstrating applications beyond molecular chemistry datasets.
summary: This paper introduces CheMLFlow, an open-source platform designed to solve the reproducibility crisis in scientific machine learning. It allows researchers to build end-to-end, automated pipelines for tasks like predicting material properties or bioactivity using molecular data. By standardizing workflows and supporting agentic experimentation, it significantly reduces manual orchestration overhead.
main_problem: The core problem addressed is the bottleneck in scientific machine learning development, where researchers struggle to assemble reproducible, end-to-end pipelines for complex tasks.
main_result: CheMLFlow provides an open-source, modular platform that standardizes and automates the entire ML workflow—from data acquisition to final reporting—for cheminformatics and materials informatics applications.
method: The authors introduce CheMLFlow, a configuration-driven framework using YAML/JSON files to orchestrate sequential or parallel computational nodes (e.g., featurization, training, validation).
model_or_system: The platform is designed for molecular and material systems, enabling high-throughput screening and benchmarking across various ML models (e.g., Random Forest, Deep Learning) applied to tasks like bioactivity prediction.
key_observables: Model performance metrics ($	ext{R}^2$, $	ext{RMSE}$, $	ext{AUROC}$), standardized run artifacts, SHAP explanations, and structured reports.
important_parameters: The platform supports varying parameters through a Design of Experiments (DOE) layer, allowing systematic testing of different representations or model settings.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that standardizing the workflow orchestration process will significantly reduce overhead and improve reproducibility across diverse scientific domains.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the three layers of CheMLFlow (Core, DOE, Agentic). Figure 2 illustrates the YAML/JSON configuration structure. Figure 3 maps a typical bioactivity prediction workflow flowchart.
paper_structure: The paper describes the system architecture by detailing its modular components: data handling, feature engineering nodes, model backends, and the overarching control flow managed by the run configuration file, culminating in benchmarking results.
why_interesting: While not focused on fundamental quantum physics, the platform's emphasis on structured, reproducible pipelines and agentic workflows is highly relevant for automating complex simulations or data analysis involving quantum chemistry calculations.
